title: Deep-network encoding models reveal a complexity hierarchy in auditory cortex
summary: Intracerebral recordings from 20 epilepsy-surgery patients listening to natural sounds were modelled with representations from layers of a deep neural network pretrained to categorise sounds. The depth of the best-fitting layer tracked anatomy, with shallow, middle and deep layers mapping to core, lateral belt and parabelt regions, with smooth gradients within regions. Sites that began encoding later had higher representational complexity independent of region. The network serves as an analysis lens in a small patient sample.
ai_technology: Encoding models using layers of a pretrained sound-categorisation deep neural network

evidence.tested: Prediction of neural responses in 20 patient-participants with intracerebral electrodes.
evidence.unknown: Generalisation beyond epilepsy patients and the causal role of the layers; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained deep network supplied the feature representations used to predict neural responses.
